IDEA: LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ
TITLE: SIDs quantised from the Lorentzian centre of mass of an item's successor-profile twins.
MOTIVATION: Two items can be behaviourally interchangeable (their next-item distributions match) while living far apart in content space, so the Euclidean RQ-VAE gives them unrelated level-1 prefixes; the Stage-3 generator then cannot use "this is an X-intent item" as a cheap first token. Stage-3 Recall@10 suffers because the first SID token carries content similarity, not behavioural role, and issue #126 measured that the hard hyperbolic first-level prefix score Q_H ranks with downstream test_R@10 (rho=+0.821). The gap addressed: make the *position that is quantised* a behaviour-consensus position, not a single item's content vector.
NOVELTY: Every earlier round touched assignment mass (Poincare Sinkhorn/OT, cocond-markov-poincare-ot), codebook updates (Poincare-Frechet, Karcher mass), curvature-from-branching (KAPPA_BRANCH), residual transport/charts (SUCC-TAN, behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts) or a post-hoc prefix-rank proxy (issue #126). None changed *which point enters the quantiser*. This idea replaces the item's latent by its Lorentzian weighted midpoint over a successor-PROFILE-equivalence neighbourhood (Hellinger similarity of transition rows), so behaviour acts on the geometry of the input, and the same curvature kappa that forms that midpoint also defines the assignment metric. It also differs from a GNN feature-smoothing trick because the smoothing is not a preprocessing of features: it is the exp/log/pseudosphere arithmetic that produces the residual chain, and the codebooks themselves live on the same hyperboloid.
CHANGE: Lift the encoder output to the hyperboloid, replace it by a 50/50 Minkowski convex combination with its K successor-profile twins, re-project onto the hyperboloid, and run the whole residual-quantisation chain (assignment by Lorentzian distance, residual by log_0) on that smoothed point.
SPECIFICATION: see SPEC EQUATIONS; kappa=1 (documented default, one unit of curvature in latent units), alpha=0.5 (equal trust between own content and behaviour twins, documented default), K=round(median positive out-degree) measured from the training transition matrix, neighbours from Hellinger/cosine similarity of row-normalised training transition profiles, all frozen before Stage 2.
COST: per step at the frozen scale (B=ceil(24556/24)=1023 items, L residual levels, C codes per level, latent d, K neighbours): smoothing gather+combine B*K*(d+1) ~ 2.7e5 MACs (K=8,d=32) = ~1% of the B*L*C*d ~ 2.5e7 MAC of the existing assignment; the Lorentzian assignment costs the same order as the Euclidean one it replaces (B*L*C*(d+1) vs B*L*C*d), so the step overhead is <2% of the quantiser and well under 1% of a full Stage-2 step. One extra no-gradient encoder pass per epoch to refresh the neighbour table (24 batches) is +4.2% encoder forward per epoch. One-off graph build from a sparse 24556x24556 transition matrix (P P^T over ~5e5 nnz rows) costs 1-3 min CPU and a few hundred MB, once, before training. Total wall-clock: baseline + ~5%.
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviourally interchangeable items should share the level-1 token, then smoothing the quantiser input along successor-profile edges will raise the fraction of successor-linked pairs sharing a level-1 code and raise the issue-#126 Q_H of the new SIDs, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 will exceed 0.065 in the single frozen run. Observed via: level-1 prefix purity against the dominant-successor label, Q_H recomputed on the new SIDs, and the one Stage-3 test_recall@10.
RISKS: (a) smoothing can wash out content identity, raising reconstruction error enough that the SID carries little item-specific information and Stage 3 loses precision; (b) the transition graph is sparse and popularity-skewed, so the twin sets are noisy and hub items dominate the consensus; (c) alpha=0.5 may be the wrong trust balance, and since no sweep is allowed it must be right first time; (d) per-epoch staleness of the neighbour table could make the smoothed point lag the encoder.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: successor-profile equivalence, i.e. the Hellinger/cosine similarity between the row-normalised directed-transition distributions of two items.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: count directed gap-1 item transitions T_ij over training sequences of the 24556 training items; row-normalise P_i. = T_i./sum_j T_ij (zero rows stay zero); s_ij = <sqrt(P_i.), sqrt(P_j.)> / (||sqrt(P_i.)|| ||sqrt(P_j.)||) clipped at 0, s_ii=0; keep the top-K per item with K = round(median positive out-degree); w_ij = s_ij / sum_{j' in N_i} s_ij'. Built once, frozen, no gradient.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: T is counted only from training-split interactions over the 24556 training items; the neighbour table, K and w are frozen before Stage 2 starts; validation and test interactions are never read by this module, and no statistic of the graph is fitted on any held-out split; the codebook, curvature and smoothing are trained only through Stage-2 reconstruction on training items.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Lorentz (hyperboloid) model L^d_kappa = {x in R^{d+1}: <x,x>_L = -1/kappa, x_0>0} with fixed negative curvature -kappa, kappa=1: exp_0, log_0, pseudosphere re-projection, and the Lorentzian distance d_H(x,y) = (1/sqrt(kappa)) arcosh(-kappa <x,y>_L), plus a Minkowski-ambient convex combination followed by re-projection (the exact Lorentzian weighted midpoint for two points).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In quantisation and in the encoder-to-quantiser interface of Stage 2: the lift, the behaviour consensus point, the codebook parameterisation, the assignment cost and the residual chain are all on the hyperboloid; the decoder maps back with log_0.
COUPLING PATH: training transitions -> successor-profile twins and weights w -> Minkowski combination of the item's and its twins' hyperboloid points -> re-projected point -> log_0 -> level-1 residual chain -> Lorentzian argmin -> SID digit 1..L -> Stage-3 sequence. COUPLING EQUATION: xhat_i = proj_kappa( (1-alpha) * exp_0^kappa(z_i) + alpha * sum_{j in N_i} w_ij * exp_0^kappa(z_j) ),  q_1(i) = argmin_k d_H( exp_0^kappa(log_0^kappa(xhat_i)), e_{1,k} )^2, with w from successor-profile similarity (behaviour term) and d_H / exp_0 / log_0 (curved term) in the same expression.
OBSERVABLES: level-1 prefix purity w.r.t. dominant successor; share of successor-linked item pairs landing in the same level-1 code; the issue-#126 hard hyperbolic prefix score Q_H recomputed on the new SIDs; codebook usage entropy per level; reconstruction loss curve; and the single Stage-3 test_recall@10 (target >0.065).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: alpha=0 and w=0 in the consensus step, so xhat_i = exp_0(z_i); the Lorentzian chain, codebooks and curvature are untouched. Code exists and is correct; not trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: kappa->0: identity lift, Euclidean consensus xhat_i = (1-alpha) z_i + alpha sum_j w_ij z_j with the same twins, L2 assignment and linear residual r_{l+1} = r_l - e_{l,q_l}. Code exists and is correct; not trained in this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: alpha=0.5, w from successor profiles, kappa=1, Lorentzian chain - this is the single trained arm.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  ambient: <x,y>_L = -x_0 y_0 + sum_{i=1..d} x_i y_i ;  proj_kappa(y) = y / sqrt(-kappa <y,y>_L)  (require <y,y>_L < 0)
  exp_0^kappa(v) = ( cosh(sqrt(kappa)||v||), sinh(sqrt(kappa)||v||) * v / (sqrt(kappa)||v||) ), v padded with leading 0
  log_0^kappa(x) = arcosh(sqrt(kappa) x_0) * x_{1:} / (sqrt(kappa) ||x_{1:}||)
  d_H(x,y)^2 = (1/kappa) * arcosh( clamp(-kappa <x,y>_L, 1+1e-7, inf) )^2
  behaviour: T_ij = # directed gap-1 transitions i->j in training sequences; P_i. = T_i. / sum_j T_ij
             s_ij = cos( sqrt(P_i.), sqrt(P_j.) ) clipped to [0,1], s_ii = 0
             N_i = topK_j s_ij, K = round(median_i outdeg_i), w_ij = s_ij / sum_{j' in N_i} s_ij'
  consensus: X_i = proj_kappa( 0.5 * exp_0^kappa(z_i) + 0.5 * sum_{j in N_i} w_ij * M_j )   with M_j = detached encoder point of j from the epoch-start table; if sum_j w_ij = 0 use X_i = exp_0^kappa(z_i)
  chain: r_1 = log_0^kappa(X_i); for l=1..L: p_l = exp_0^kappa(r_l); q_l = argmin_k d_H(p_l, e_{l,k})^2; r_{l+1} = r_l - log_0^kappa(e_{l,q_l})
  reconstruction: zhat_i = sum_{l=1..L} log_0^kappa(e_{l,q_l}); loss = ||zhat_i - z_i||^2 + straight-through commitment/codebook terms exactly as in the baseline RQ-VAE (unchanged)
  epoch table refresh: after each epoch, for all 24556 items, M_i <- proj_kappa(exp_0^kappa(encoder(x_i))) with no gradient, 24 batches.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: in - item content features x_i, the frozen K-NN successor-profile graph (indices + weights), encoder parameters, codebook parameters, kappa, alpha, L, C. out - for each item the L SID digits, the quantised tangent vector zhat_i, and gradients to the encoder, the codebooks and (through the assignment) the consensus point.
SAFEGUARDS: (1) clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7 and the tangent norm to atanh(1-1e-5)/sqrt(kappa) before every exp so points never reach the boundary; (2) re-project onto the hyperboloid after every addition/multiplication; the future timelike cone is convex so a convex combination of valid points stays timelike and the projection is always defined - assert <y,y>_L <= -1e-6 and fall back to the self-point otherwise; (3) zero-out and renormalise rows with sum_j w_ij = 0 or with NaN similarity; (4) drop exact-duplicate twins so an item cannot average with itself; (5) compute d_H in float64 for the arcosh branch to avoid gradient blow-up near coincidence; (6) initialise codebooks with the baseline Euclidean codebook lifted by exp_0 so the first step matches the baseline geometry; (7) keep the behaviour graph in a frozen buffer and assert its mtime/hash matches the pre-Stage-2 snapshot (leak guard).
END IDEA

END RECORD.`});

NOVELTY: Every earlier round touched assignment mass (Poincare Sinkhorn/OT, cocond-markov-poincare-ot), codebook updates (Poincare-Frechet, Karcher mass), curvature-from-branching (KAPPA_BRANCH), residual transport/charts (SUCC-TAN, behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts) or a post-hoc prefix-rank proxy (issue #126). None changed *which point enters the quantiser*. This idea replaces the item's latent by its Lorentzian weighted midpoint over a successor-PROFILE-equivalence neighbourhood (Hellinger similarity of transition rows), so behaviour acts on the geometry of the input, and the same curvature kappa that forms that midpoint also defines the assignment metric. It also differs from a GNN feature-smoothing trick because the smoothing is not a preprocessing of features: it is the exp/log/pseudosphere arithmetic that produces the residual chain, and the codebooks themselves live on the same hyperboloid.
CHANGE: Lift the encoder output to the hyperboloid, replace it by a 50/50 Minkowski convex combination with its K successor-profile twins, re-project onto the hyperboloid, and run the whole residual-quantisation chain (assignment by Lorentzian distance, residual by log_0) on that smoothed point.
SPECIFICATION: see SPEC EQUATIONS; kappa=1 (documented default, one unit of curvature in latent units), alpha=0.5 (equal trust between own content and behaviour twins, documented default), K=round(median positive out-degree) measured from the training transition matrix, neighbours from Hellinger/cosine similarity of row-normalised training transition profiles, all frozen before Stage 2.
COST: per step at the frozen scale (B=ceil(24556/24)=1023 items, L residual levels, C codes per level, latent d, K neighbours): smoothing gather+combine B*K*(d+1) ~ 2.7e5 MACs (K=8,d=32) = ~1% of the B*L*C*d ~ 2.5e7 MAC of the existing assignment; the Lorentzian assignment costs the same order as the Euclidean one it replaces (B*L*C*(d+1) vs B*L*C*d), so the step overhead is <2% of the quantiser and well under 1% of a full Stage-2 step. One extra no-gradient encoder pass per epoch to refresh the neighbour table (24 batches) is +4.2% encoder forward per epoch. One-off graph build from a sparse 24556x24556 transition matrix (P P^T over ~5e5 nnz rows) costs 1-3 min CPU and a few hundred MB, once, before training. Total wall-clock: baseline + ~5%.
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviourally interchangeable items should share the level-1 token, then smoothing the quantiser input along successor-profile edges will raise the fraction of successor-linked pairs sharing a level-1 code and raise the issue-#126 Q_H of the new SIDs, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 will exceed 0.065 in the single frozen run. Observed via: level-1 prefix purity against the dominant-successor label, Q_H recomputed on the new SIDs, and the one Stage-3 test_recall@10.
RISKS: (a) smoothing can wash out content identity, raising reconstruction error enough that the SID carries little item-specific information and Stage 3 loses precision; (b) the transition graph is sparse and popularity-skewed, so the twin sets are noisy and hub items dominate the consensus; (c) alpha=0.5 may be the wrong trust balance, and since no sweep is allowed it must be right first time; (d) per-epoch staleness of the neighbour table could make the smoothed point lag the encoder.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: successor-profile equivalence, i.e. the Hellinger/cosine similarity between the row-normalised directed-transition distributions of two items.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: count directed gap-1 item transitions T_ij over training sequences of the 24556 training items; row-normalise P_i. = T_i./sum_j T_ij (zero rows stay zero); s_ij = <sqrt(P_i.), sqrt(P_j.)> / (||sqrt(P_i.)|| ||sqrt(P_j.)||) clipped at 0, s_ii=0; keep the top-K per item with K = round(median positive out-degree); w_ij = s_ij / sum_{j' in N_i} s_ij'. Built once, frozen, no gradient.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: T is counted only from training-split interactions over the 24556 training items; the neighbour table, K and w are frozen before Stage 2 starts; validation and test interactions are never read by this module, and no statistic of the graph is fitted on any held-out split; the codebook, curvature and smoothing are trained only through Stage-2 reconstruction on training items.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Lorentz (hyperboloid) model L^d_kappa = {x in R^{d+1}: <x,x>_L = -1/kappa, x_0>0} with fixed negative curvature -kappa, kappa=1: exp_0, log_0, pseudosphere re-projection, and the Lorentzian distance d_H(x,y) = (1/sqrt(kappa)) arcosh(-kappa <x,y>_L), plus a Minkowski-ambient convex combination followed by re-projection (the exact Lorentzian weighted midpoint for two points).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In quantisation and in the encoder-to-quantiser interface of Stage 2: the lift, the behaviour consensus point, the codebook parameterisation, the assignment cost and the residual chain are all on the hyperboloid; the decoder maps back with log_0.
COUPLING PATH: training transitions -> successor-profile twins and weights w -> Minkowski combination of the item's and its twins' hyperboloid points -> re-projected point -> log_0 -> level-1 residual chain -> Lorentzian argmin -> SID digit 1..L -> Stage-3 sequence. Removing the behaviour term (alpha=0, w=0) puts the raw item point into the same curved chain; removing the geometry (kappa->0, Euclidean lift, Euclidean mean, L2 assignment) keeps the same twins but changes both the consensus point and every assignment. Both switches therefore change the SID assignment itself, not an accessory loss.
COUPLING EQUATION: xhat_i = proj_kappa( (1-alpha) * exp_0^kappa(z_i) + alpha * sum_{j in N_i} w_ij * exp_0^kappa(z_j) ),  q_1(i) = argmin_k d_H( exp_0^kappa(log_0^kappa(xhat_i)), e_{1,k} )^2, with w from successor-profile similarity (behaviour term) and d_H / exp_0 / log_0 (curved term) in the same expression.
OBSERVABLES: level-1 prefix purity w.r.t. dominant successor; share of successor-linked item pairs landing in the same level-1 code; the issue-#126 hard hyperbolic prefix score Q_H recomputed on the new SIDs; codebook usage entropy per level; reconstruction loss curve; and the single Stage-3 test_recall@10 (target >0.065).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: alpha=0 and w=0 in the consensus step, so xhat_i = exp_0(z_i); the Lorentzian chain, codebooks and curvature are untouched. Code exists and is correct; not trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: kappa->0: identity lift, Euclidean consensus xhat_i = (1-alpha) z_i + alpha sum_j w_ij z_j with the same twins, L2 assignment and linear residual r_{l+1} = r_l - e_{l,q_l}. Code exists and is correct; not trained in this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: alpha=0.5, w from successor profiles, kappa=1, Lorentzian chain - this is the single trained arm.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  ambient: <x,y>_L = -x_0 y_0 + sum_{i=1..d} x_i y_i ;  proj_kappa(y) = y / sqrt(-kappa <y,y>_L)  (require <y,y>_L < 0)
  exp_0^kappa(v) = ( cosh(sqrt(kappa)||v||), sinh(sqrt(kappa)||v||) * v / (sqrt(kappa)||v||) ), v padded with leading 0
  log_0^kappa(x) = arcosh(sqrt(kappa) x_0) * x_{1:} / (sqrt(kappa) ||x_{1:}||)
  d_H(x,y)^2 = (1/kappa) * arcosh( clamp(-kappa <x,y>_L, 1+1e-7, inf) )^2
  behaviour: T_ij = # directed gap-1 transitions i->j in training sequences; P_i. = T_i. / sum_j T_ij
             s_ij = cos( sqrt(P_i.), sqrt(P_j.) ) clipped to [0,1], s_ii = 0
             N_i = topK_j s_ij, K = round(median_i outdeg_i), w_ij = s_ij / sum_{j' in N_i} s_ij'
  consensus: X_i = proj_kappa( 0.5 * exp_0^kappa(z_i) + 0.5 * sum_{j in N_i} w_ij * M_j )   with M_j = detached encoder point of j from the epoch-start table; if sum_j w_ij = 0 use X_i = exp_0^kappa(z_i)

  reconstruction: zhat_i = sum_{l=1..L} log_0^kappa(e_{l,q_l}); loss = ||zhat_i - z_i||^2 + straight-through commitment/codebook terms exactly as in the baseline RQ-VAE (unchanged)
  epoch table refresh: after each epoch, for all 24556 items, M_i <- proj_kappa(exp_0^kappa(encoder(x_i))) with no gradient, 24 batches.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: in - item content features x_i, the frozen K-NN successor-profile graph (indices + weights), encoder parameters, codebook parameters, kappa, alpha, L, C. out - for each item the L SID digits, the quantised tangent vector zhat_i, and gradients to the encoder, the codebooks and (through the assignment) the consensus point.
SAFEGUARDS: (1) clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7 and the tangent norm to atanh(1-1e-5)/sqrt(kappa) before every exp so points never reach the boundary; (2) re-project onto the hyperboloid after every addition/multiplication; the future timelike cone is convex so a convex combination of valid points stays timelike and the projection is always defined - assert <y,y>_L <= -1e-6 and fall back to the self-point otherwise; (3) zero-out and renormalise rows with sum_j w_ij = 0 or with NaN similarity; (4) drop exact-duplicate twins so an item cannot average with itself; (5) compute d_H in float64 for the arcosh branch to avoid gradient blow-up near coincidence; (6) initialise codebooks with the baseline Euclidean codebook lifted by exp_0 so the first step matches the baseline geometry; (7) keep the behaviour graph in a frozen buffer and assert its mtime/hash matches the pre-Stage-2 snapshot (leak guard).
END IDEA

END RECORD.`});
return [a, b];"}

IDEA: LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ
TITLE: SIDs quantised from the Lorentzian centre of mass of an item's successor-profile twins
MOTIVATION: Two items can be behaviourally interchangeable — their next-item distributions match — while sitting far apart in content space, so a Euclidean RQ-VAE hands them unrelated level-1 prefixes and the Stage-3 generator cannot use "this is an X-intent item" as a cheap first token. Issue #126 measured that the hard hyperbolic first-level prefix score Q_H ranks with downstream test_R@10 (Spearman +0.821, small sample), which says the level-1 partition, not the deeper digits, is where recall is decided. The unaddressed gap: the point that actually enters the quantiser is a single item's content vector, never a behaviour-consensus position, so behaviourally equivalent items cannot be pulled into one cell at the level that matters.
NOVELTY: The earlier rounds occupied (i) soft/OT assignment mass, (ii) codebook centroid updates (Fréchet/Karcher), (iii) curvature as a function of branching, (iv) residual transport and geodesic charts, (v) a post-hoc prefix-rank proxy. None of them changed *which point is quantised*. Here the behaviour signal is moved upstream into the geometry of the quantiser input: the item's hyperboloid point is replaced by its Lorentzian weighted midpoint over a successor-PROFILE-equivalence neighbourhood, and the same curvature that forms that midpoint also defines the assignment metric and the residual chain. It also differs from a GNN feature-smoothing trick: the smoothing is not preprocessing of features, it is the exp/log/pseudosphere arithmetic that generates the residual chain, and the codebooks live on the same hyperboloid. The behaviour relation is successor-profile similarity (Hellinger/cosine of row-normalised transition rows), not raw directed edges — raw edges, which every earlier round used, conflate "co-occurs with" with "behaves alike".
CHANGE: Lift the encoder output to the hyperboloid, replace it by a 50/50 Minkowski convex combination with its K successor-profile twins, re-project onto the hyperboloid, and run the entire residual-quantisation chain (Lorentzian-distance assignment, log_0 residual) on that smoothed point.
SPECIFICATION: kappa = 1 (documented default: one unit of curvature in latent units), alpha = 0.5 (documented default: equal trust between own content and behaviour twins), K = round(median positive out-degree) measured from the training transition matrix, twins from cosine similarity of sqrt of row-normalised training transition profiles, whole graph frozen before Stage 2; full equations in SPEC EQUATIONS.
COST: Frozen scale, B = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items per step, L levels, C codes per level, latent d = 32, K neighbours. Smoothing gather/combine B*K*(d+1) ≈ 1023*8*33 ≈ 2.7e5 MAC per step ≈ 1% of the existing B*L*C*d ≈ 1023*3*256*32 ≈ 2.5e7 MAC assignment. The Lorentzian assignment replaces the Euclidean one at the same order (B*L*C*(d+1) vs B*L*C*d), so step overhead is under 2% of the quantiser and under 1% of a full Stage-2 step; the epoch-start table refresh is one no-gradient encoder pass (24 batches) = +4.2% encoder forward per epoch. One-off graph build (sparse P·Pᵀ on a 24556×24556 transition matrix, ~5e5 nnz) is 1–3 min CPU, a few hundred MB, once. Over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72k steps this is baseline + ~5% wall clock, no memory growth.
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviourally interchangeable items should share the level-1 token, then smoothing the quantiser input along successor-profile edges will (a) raise the share of successor-linked pairs that share a level-1 code, (b) raise the issue-#126 Q_H recomputed on the new SIDs, and (c) push the single frozen Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Observed through the three diagnostics plus the one test run; if Q_H rises but recall does not, the level-1 partition is not the binding constraint.

BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only, count directed gap-1 item transitions T_ij over the training sequences of the 24556 training items; row-normalise P_i· = T_i· / Σ_j T_ij (zero rows stay zero); s_ij = ⟨√P_i·, √P_j·⟩ / (‖√P_i·‖‖√P_j·‖) clipped to [0,1], with s_ii = 0; keep the top-K per item, K = round(median_i outdeg_i); w_ij = s_ij / Σ_{j'∈N_i} s_ij'. Built once, frozen, no gradient, no parameters.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: T is counted only from training-split interactions over the 24556 training items. The twin table, K and w are frozen and hashed before Stage 2 starts, and the hash is asserted on every epoch; validation and test interactions are never read by this module and no statistic of the graph is fitted on any held-out split.   exp_0^kappa(v) = ( cosh(√kappa‖v‖), sinh(√kappa‖v‖)·v / (√kappa‖v‖) ), with v embedded with leading 0
  log_0^kappa(x) = arcosh(√kappa·x_0) · x_{1:} / (√kappa‖x_{1:}‖)
  d_H(x,y)² = (1/kappa)·arcosh( clamp(−kappa⟨x,y⟩_L, 1+1e-7, ∞) )²

             N_i = topK_j s_ij, K = round(median_i outdeg_i), w_ij = s_ij / Σ_{j'∈N_i} s_ij'
  consensus: X_i = proj_kappa( 0.5·exp_0^kappa(z_i) + 0.5·Σ_{j∈N_i} w_ij·M_j ), M_j = detached hyperboloid point of j from the epoch-start table; if Σ_j w_ij = 0 then X_i = exp_0^kappa(z_i)
  chain: r_1 = log_0^kappa(X_i); for l = 1..L: p_l = exp_0^kappa(r_l); q_l = argmin_k d_H(p_l, e_{l,k})²; r_{l+1} = r_l − log_0^kappa(e_{l,q_l})
